interpretation: The collector samples faster than the agent writes, and the staleness window carries one agent row forward into several samples. The paired-row count is therefore a property of the recorder's cadence, not of the agent. Any statistic computed over the nominal count would score the staleness window.
why_the_obvious_fix_is_forbidden: Widening max_age raises the nominal pair count and lowers the effective one — it makes the contamination worse while making the harness look healthier. That is the exact failure class of SYNTHESIS_recorder_contamination_2026_08_06.md. The correct fix is to emit a bin only when the agent row is NEW, which cannot inflate n because it cannot produce more bins than the agent produced rows.

duplicate_instances_found.effect: Two independent processes each sampling every 60s and appending to ONE store, which is why the measured sample rate is 120/h against an intended 60/h. Each carried the same stale agent row forward independently, so the duplication is multiplicative with the staleness-window defect, not additive.
duplicate_instances_found.note: Found 2026-08-08 while auditing; neither instance was aware of the other.

changes: consolidated to a single collector process
agent rows deduplicated by payload: a carried-forward row now records as a gap
remediation.IMPORTANT: The store spans TWO regimes. Rows before cutover_unix_ts are contaminated -- 92% duplicate agent payloads, effective n at most 4, and double-written by two processes. Any analysis MUST split on this timestamp and must not pool across it. No R1-v2 analysis has been run on the pre-cutover data.
remediation.expected_effect: The dedup filter cannot emit more rows than the agent wrote, so nominal n should fall to at most the agent's write count and n_inflation_factor should approach 1.0. Verify by re-running this audit on post-cutover rows.
